chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about pelting the Jamarah on the Day of Nahr (Sacrifice), 'What is the matter with it that it is pelted alone, and the other Jamarat are not pelted on the Day of Nahr?' So he said: 'All of them used to be pelted, but they left that.' So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so can I pelt them all?' He said: 'Do not pelt them all. Are you not pleased that you do similar to what we do?'

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)
key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجَمْرَةِ: Pelting the Jamarah (ritual throwing of pebbles)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Why is only one Jamarah pelted on the Day of Nahr during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *ittiba’* (following the Imams) in ritual practice, where the Prophet’s Sunnah was refined by the Imams to establish a specific legal norm. It clarifies that while pelting all pillars was historically practiced, the Imams restricted the Day of Nahr ritual to the Jamarat al-Kubra, instructing believers to emulate this precise action as a sign of adherence to their authority. This distinction underscores the dynamic nature of Shia fiqh, where ritual details are preserved and transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt.
